title: Counterexample Set
html: The counterexample set of an argument form is the list of its premises together with the negation of its conclusion. A counterexample to the form is an argument of that form whose premises are all true and whose conclusion is false, that is, a choice of statements for the letters that makes every member of the counterexample set true. A form is bad if it has a counterexample, and good if no choice of statements can break it.
